title: After Jensen Huang: What Founder Exits Did to Apple, Alphabet and Uber
excerpt: Nvidia's co-founder resigned with no named successor and no reason given. The record of Apple, Alphabet, Uber and Twitter shows preparation — not the founder's genius — decides what happens next.
body:
• Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member effective immediately, the company announced on November 12, 2026; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones is the board's first-ever chair.
  • History cuts both ways: Apple and Alphabet grew far larger under successors Tim Cook and Sundar Pichai, while Uber needed a new chief to repair its culture and reach profitability after Travis Kalanick's 2017 exit.
  • Experts told CNBC Nvidia looks unusually exposed: Huang ran a flat structure with about 60 direct reports and, in one professor's assessment, no visible succession plan.
  • What to watch: Nvidia reports third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Tuesday, November 17, at about 1:20 p.m. PT — the first earnings test of the post-Huang company.

When a founder leaves, the company loses more than a chief executive. It loses the person who set its strategy, hired its leaders and, in the strongest cases, became its public identity. Nvidia is now running that experiment at the largest possible scale: Jensen Huang, who co-founded the chipmaker and led it for 33 years, resigned as president, CEO and board member effective immediately, Nvidia announced on November 12. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress serves as interim CEO while keeping her finance role, and the board has begun a search considering internal and external candidates.

What Nvidia has said — and what it has not

Nvidia's announcement gives no reason for the resignation. It stresses continuity: Kress has led the finance organisation since joining in September 2013, after nearly 25 years in finance roles at Cisco and Microsoft, and the board says operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap will continue without interruption.

"NVIDIA's strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years."

— Colette Kress, Interim CEO and CFO, NVIDIA

Analysts and academics are less settled. "I'm not sure we've seen a situation quite like this, where the founder and CEO of one of the world's largest companies faces such a sudden departure amid scandal," Michael Withers, a professor of management at the University of Notre Dame's Mendoza College of Business, told CNBC. Withers said successor CEOs often struggle even in normal circumstances to maintain what made a company successful while establishing their own leadership, and that Huang's flat structure — an extraordinary 60 direct reports — leaves relationships and decisions concentrated in one person. CNBC reported that Withers saw no apparent succession plan for Huang.

The successors who made it work

Apple is the strongest case that a company can outgrow its founder. Steve Jobs handed over to Tim Cook in 2011, and Cook — an operator who had run Apple's supply chain and had, in Withers' words, "considerable preparation" — invested in Apple's chip strategy and services business. Apple's market value rose from about $350 billion to $4 trillion during Cook's 15-year tenure, according to CNBC.

Alphabet followed the planned version of the same path. Larry Page and Sergey Brin left their executive roles in 2019, 21 years after founding Google, with Page calling it the "natural time" to simplify management. Alphabet shares are up more than 300% since then under Sundar Pichai, CNBC reported.

The exits that took repair work

Uber's transition was forced and slower. Travis Kalanick, who co-founded Uber in 2009 and led its global expansion, resigned in 2017 under pressure from investors after reports detailing an aggressive company culture, according to Inc. His successor, former Expedia CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, repaired the organisation and found a path to profitability; Uber went public in 2019 and today claims a market value of about $141 billion, Inc reported.

Some founders come back. Jack Dorsey was pushed out as Twitter's CEO in 2008, returned in 2015, and stepped down again in 2021, according to Inc. Sam Altman's ouster from OpenAI in 2023 lasted five days before he was reinstated. Those boomerangs underline the same point from the other side: boards reach for the founder when no successor holds the company's authority.

What decides which story Nvidia gets

The pattern across these cases is not the founder's talent but the preparation left behind. Cook and Pichai were internal successors with years of operating authority before the handover. Kalanick's Uber had no such figure and needed an outsider to rebuild it. Nvidia sits between the two: Kress is a 13-year insider, but she is interim, holds two jobs at once, and inherits a structure built around Huang personally — including, CNBC noted, his close relationships with suppliers such as SK Hynix and Samsung and with the U.S. administration on chip export restrictions.

Investors quoted by CNBC noted one stabiliser: the new CEO inherits a product roadmap set for the next few years. The first public test arrives quickly, when Nvidia reports quarterly results on November 17. For Indian-origin engineers and investors across the U.S. tech sector — heavily represented at Nvidia and across the AI industry — the succession search, and whether Kress stays interim for months or longer, is the story to follow.
